overview: Portugal is the westernmost country of mainland Europe, on the Iberian Peninsula. Its capital and largest city is Lisbon. In the 1400s and 1500s Portuguese sailors led Europe's voyages of exploration, and Portugal built an empire across Africa, Asia and South America; Portuguese is now spoken by more than 250 million people, most of them in Brazil. Portugal joined what is now the European Union in 1986.

geography.text: Mainland Portugal faces the Atlantic along a long coastline of beaches and cliffs. The north is hilly and green, while the south, especially the Algarve, is drier and sunnier. The Tagus and the Douro rivers flow west across the country from Spain to the sea. Portugal also includes two groups of Atlantic islands, the Azores and Madeira.

history.text: Portugal became an independent kingdom in the 1100s, with borders that have barely changed since. In the 1400s and 1500s its sailors explored the coasts of Africa, reached India and Brazil, and built a trading empire across the globe. A revolution in 1910 ended the monarchy, and the peaceful Carnation Revolution of 1974 ended decades of dictatorship.

events.title: Kingdom recognised
events.text: Portugal is recognised as an independent kingdom.

events.title: Sea route to India
events.text: Vasco da Gama reaches India by sailing around Africa.

events.title: Brazil reached
events.text: Pedro Álvares Cabral lands in Brazil.

events.title: Lisbon earthquake
events.text: An earthquake and tsunami destroy much of Lisbon.

events.title: Carnation Revolution
events.text: A largely peaceful military coup ends dictatorship and leads to democracy.

government.text: Portugal is a semi-presidential republic. The President, elected directly every five years, is head of state and can dissolve parliament. The Prime Minister leads the government with the support of the Assembly of the Republic. Portugal was a founding member of NATO and joined what is now the European Union in 1986.

economy.text: Tourism is a major part of Portugal's economy, alongside textiles, shoes, cork, wine and car parts. Portugal produces about half of the world's cork. In recent years it has become a popular base for technology companies and start-ups, and much of its electricity comes from renewable sources.

culture.text: Portuguese is spoken by more than 250 million people worldwide, from Brazil to Angola and Mozambique. Fado, a melancholy style of song, is on UNESCO's list of intangible heritage. Portuguese buildings are often decorated with blue-and-white painted tiles called azulejos.

items.title: Fado
items.text: Songs of longing, sung in the old quarters of Lisbon and Coimbra.

items.title: Azulejos
items.text: Painted ceramic tiles covering churches, stations and houses.

items.title: Pastéis de nata
items.text: Custard tarts first made by monks in Belém.

sport.text: Football is Portugal's great passion. Cristiano Ronaldo, born on Madeira, is the leading scorer in men's international football. Portugal won Euro 2016 and the UEFA Nations League in 2019 and 2025.

items.title: Euro 2016
items.text: Portugal beat hosts France 1–0 in the final.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo
items.text: The record goalscorer in men's international football.

items.title: Eusébio
items.text: Born in Mozambique, he starred for Portugal at the 1966 World Cup.
